title: Artificial Intelligence in Vehicular Networks: A Comprehensive Review of Security Challenges and Defenses
content: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into vehicular networks has fundamentally transformed intelligent transportation systems, enabling autonomous driving, cooperative perception, and real-time traffic management. However, this convergence has simultaneously expanded the security attack surface, creating novel vulnerabilities that traditional cryptographic defenses alone cannot address. This comprehensive review examines the intersection of AI, vehicular networks, and security, providing a systematic analysis of emerging threats and defense mechanisms. We first establish the architectural foundations of modern vehicular networks, tracing the evolution from Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) to the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) and AI-native V2X systems. We then present a multi-layered threat taxonomy encompassing traditional protocol-level attacks and AI-specific vulnerabilities, including adversarial examples, data poisoning, model inversion, and Byzantine attacks in federated learning environments. Our analysis of defense mechanisms covers machine learning-based intrusion detection systems, blockchain-assisted trust management, federated learning with privacy preservation, and adversarial robustness techniques. We identify critical research gaps, particularly the disconnection between theoretical attack demonstrations and real-world validation, the tension between privacy preservation and detection efficacy, and the unresolved challenge of securing distributed learning under non-IID vehicular data distributions. The review concludes by proposing an integrated security framework that addresses these challenges through explainable AI, adaptive defense mechanisms, and safety-certifiable architectures for next-generation vehicular systems.
